summary: Warm River Butte L-4 cab on an enclosed wooden tower in the Caribou-Targhee NF, Idaho; cabin 1942, burned 1976 per one list; a July 2011 blog post found only footings and steel.

facts.design: L-4 cab on an enclosed wooden tower
facts.status_note: Gone; one list gives 1976 as the year it burned, and a July 2011 blog post found only cement footings and jagged steel

staffing.status: named staff in 1947 and 1948; listed unstaffed by 1973

access.note: No closure notice found. The only visit report read is a July 2011 blog post, which places the butte along Fish Creek Road and describes the road on the butte as narrow and winding; no current status found

visit.trail_note: A July 2011 blog post describes the road on the butte as narrow, winding and sometimes steep, and advises against low-clearance vehicles

events.note: Cabin, per two lists; an L-4 cab on an enclosed wooden tower followed in the 1940s

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The July 1948 newspaper quotes describe a 30-foot tower, while the Idaho listing and firelookout.com give 25 feet for the 1940s cab. The story reports both, and height_m uses 30 feet from the contemporary account.
The Idaho listing spells the name Gene Hawks; the 1948 Post-Register item spells it Gene Hawkes. The story uses the newspaper spelling and says the sources differ.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checks out: gone, Caribou-Targhee NF, Fremont County, 30-foot (9.1 m) height. Lists give 25 feet for the 1940s cab, and only the 1948 newspaper quotes give 30. Elevation differs: 6615 ft (Idaho listing) vs 6054 ft (firelookout.com); not used. The 1976 burn date comes only from the Idaho listing. A Facebook post by the FFLA group, seen only as a search snippet, says possibly burned in the 1960s; not read, so not used. A 2023 Pastmaps map blurb in search results still refers to a Warm River Lookout as a vantage point; not read, and it looks generated, so not used. Access 'public' is inferred from the 2011 road account and the lack of any closure notice; verify before relying on it. The only visit account is the July 2011 blog post; no later description was found.
